title: How Many National Championships Has Oklahoma Football Won? Seven
question: How many national championships has Oklahoma football won?
answer: Oklahoma claims seven national championships: 1950, 1955 and 1956 under Bud Wilkinson; 1974, 1975 and 1985 under Barry Switzer; and 2000 under Bob Stoops.
summary: Oklahoma claims seven football national titles: 1950, 1955, 1956, 1974, 1975, 1985 and 2000. Here's each one, its coach, and the other years OU doesn't claim.
body: Ask a Sooners fan how many national titles Oklahoma has and you'll hear seven. That is the program's own count, and it covers three coaching eras.

Bud Wilkinson won the first three. The 1950 team was voted No. 1 before its Sugar Bowl loss to Kentucky. The 1955 team went 11-0 and beat Maryland in the Orange Bowl, and the 1956 team went 10-0 and sat out bowl season under the Big Seven's no-repeat rule.

Barry Switzer added three more. His 1974 team went unbeaten while banned from bowl games, the 1975 team beat Michigan in the Orange Bowl, and the 1985 team beat top-ranked Penn State 25-10 in Miami for what became the program's sixth title.
Bob Stoops brought home number seven. The 2000 Sooners finished 13-0 by beating Florida State 13-2 in the Orange Bowl on Jan. 3, 2001, which made OU the only unbeaten team in the country that year.

Some lists you'll find online give Oklahoma more. Over the years various selectors have named the Sooners champions in other seasons, including 1915, 1949, 1953, 1957, 1967, 1973, 1978, 1980, 1986 and 2003. Oklahoma doesn't count those, so seven remains the official answer for trivia night.
